open_points.subject: CLK-002 operation scope and wall-clock reading count
open_points.text: “an operation takes one wall reading” conflicts with “a test per operation that reads the wall clock” and with the earlier rule that an operation reads the clock “for its own timestamps”; the text also says “where in an operation its one clock read happens” is carried to States 6–7.
open_points.question: Which requests or use-case paths count as operations that must take exactly one wall reading, which take none, and at what precise point—including on refusal paths—is that reading taken?
options: Every operation, including read-only health and early-refusal paths, takes one wall reading.
Only an operation that writes a timestamp or performs a current-time comparison takes one wall reading.
A request may take no reading if it is refused before a specified clock-read point.
open_points.default_guess: Require one wall reading only on paths that need a portal-owned timestamp or current-time comparison, after validations that require no current time.

witness.initial: The wall-clock source is a counting source; the service has a public liveness operation that writes no timestamp and performs no expiry comparison.
events: The test or operator inspects the source's read count.
outcomes: CLK-002 is read literally: the operation takes one wall reading.
The normative qualification and Required test are followed: the operation takes no wall reading.
witness.observer: The clock-policy test or host operator instrumenting clock reads.

open_points.subject: Accepted forms of source-supplied datetimes
open_points.text: Source-supplied times are stored as “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC,” but “their accepted forms and checks” are carried to States 6–7.
open_points.question: Must each source-supplied datetime contain an offset, or may an offset-naive datetime be accepted; if it is accepted, what instant does it denote?
options: Accept an offset-naive value as already UTC.
Accept it using some source-specific timezone rule.
open_points.default_guess: Reject offset-naive source-supplied datetimes because they do not identify an instant.

witness.initial: An active producer has permission to import a snapshot.
events: The producer submits an otherwise valid snapshot whose approved_at is 2026-11-08T10:00:00 with no offset.
outcomes: The import is refused because the supplied datetime does not identify an instant.
The import is accepted and approved_at is stored as offset-naive 2026-11-08T10:00:00, interpreted as UTC.
witness.observer: The producer and a later reader of the stored snapshot.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 Required-test witness
open_points.text: The Required tests bind only “CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]” and “CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal]”; no `[witness: ...]` is bound to CLK-002.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its sole-host-clock-reader, exact-read-count, fixed-instant validity, and elapsed-clock restrictions?
options: Bind CLK-002 to one existing verification check covering all its required cases.
Bind its wall-clock and elapsed-clock obligations to separate existing checks.
open_points.default_guess: Use separate wall-clock and viewer-entry elapsed-clock checks and bind both explicitly to CLK-002.

open_points.subject: OSV export readability and completeness gate
open_points.text: The archive is complete when “the archive's index reads without error,” while every installed distribution is judged against it and “a check that cannot complete does not pass”; neither “index” nor the required validation of indexed advisory members is defined.
open_points.question: What exactly must be read successfully before the OSV copy is usable: only the archive directory/index, every archive member, every OSV entry, or only entries determined to name installed distributions?
options: A readable archive directory/index is sufficient; malformed advisory members are handled only if selected later.
Every member and OSV entry must be readable, even for packages not installed.
Only entries identified as naming installed distributions must be readable; malformed unrelated entries are ignored.
open_points.default_guess: Require every archive member and OSV entry to be readable so the checker can establish which entries name installed distributions.

witness.initial: The downloaded archive has the announced length and a readable archive directory; one advisory member is corrupt, and the image contains no distribution that the member's filename appears to name.
events: The deploy gate opens the archive and evaluates the image.
The gate reaches or skips the corrupt member.
outcomes: The deploy is blocked because the one-copy check cannot completely read the OSV data.
The deploy starts because the archive index is readable and the corrupt member is treated as irrelevant to installed distributions.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and service users waiting for the new image.

open_points.subject: Deployment tool handoff
open_points.text: “The tool that runs the check is a deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the deploy route.”
open_points.question: Which receiving state owns the deployment-gate execution, what decided interface or procedure performs it, and which check confirms that the exact image digest, installed-distribution inventory, one fresh OSV copy, and verdict stay bound together?
options: A named later state receives a specified release-gate contract and verification check.
State 2 selects the concrete deployment tool and records its check here.
The deploy-route implementer chooses the tool and binding mechanism without another design decision.
open_points.default_guess: Carry a tool-independent but exact release-gate contract to a named deployment state with the existing DEP-002 verification as its check.
